brief: Universal: any company, any person, found with Apollo's search. No scoring rubric and no harvest: a person searches Apollo on the Universal page, ticks the people or companies worth keeping, and saves them here as leads. Everything after that -- shortlisting, rejecting, contacts, export -- is the same as every other project, and since 2026-09-27 a person can write an email to the leads they pick (outreach.compose).

sources.name: Apollo.io API (people and company search, bulk people reveal)
sources.detail: tools/apollo.py, from the Universal page. People search is free and returns a preview (first name, masked last name, title, employer). Saving a person reveals them with people/bulk_match: 1 credit per person Apollo holds data for. Company search is 1 credit per page. Key: APOLLO_API_KEY in .env and in Render's Environment tab.

self_exclusion.guidance: TVF and its affiliates never enter the lead pool, from any source. An Apollo search can return TVF's own people and companies; saving one is refused, the same way the promote chain refuses them for the other segments. Domains match on the host or a subdomain, name patterns as whole words.

sender.guidance: Sender name and title for the shared sign-off. The address is retained as an optional footer field and omitted from the default email footer (owner, 2026-10-09). The sending address comes from the connected Gmail account.

send_window.guidance: Owner, 2026-10-12: "I want you to send mails to the sender's time region between 10 to 10:30AM and that must be randmized not like all mail going at 10:15 some must be going at 10:17 some at 10:13 and so on after approval implement it". Each approved email goes out at its own random second between start and end on its RECIPIENT's clock (10:00 in Mumbai is 05:30 in London, too early to be read), drawn when it is approved and shown in Approved as "Goes out", with the time in India beside it. Where the recipient is comes from what the lead holds -- the person's own Apollo record, the company's state or city, a phone's area code, its country -- and the reason is kept on the email (tools/send_window.py). Monday to Friday on the recipient's clock (weekdays_only): an approval after today's window, or at a weekend, takes the next weekday's. An email whose window passes unsent (the server down, its address at its daily limit) moves to the next window at a new random time, never later the same day. Never two emails from one address closer than min_gap_seconds; never one sooner than min_lead_seconds after its approval. To send on the sender's clock instead (every email 10:00-10:30 India time) set timezone_of to "sender"; to switch the window off set enabled to false -- the stored times are cleared and approvals go out as soon as they can, as before. docs/runbook.md, "Goes out". Each written email is placed when its writer approves it (Write email); a lead that names no place goes at India's 10:00 (fallback_timezone).

footer.guidance: Owner decision 2026-10-09: the sign-off, with the postal address omitted. The owner, 2026-10-13: the opt-out line is removed from every project's footer ("remove the last line from every single service"); any reply that is not neutral still stops all mail to that address. Edited in Outreach -> Footer. Postal addresses are optional; templates end with {{footer}}.

outreach.default_cc_guidance: The owner, 2026-10-22: "add a feature to cc someone from the software itself. Make default cc to the email amritanshv@lightscameraexperiment.com and obvio make a toggle to switch that off". Every email of this project is copied to these addresses unless the person approving it switches that off in the email (the CC toggle) or changes the list. The list an email is approved with is the one it goes out with (outreach.cc, sql/39, frozen at approval): changing this default never changes an email already approved. A reply from one of these addresses is not taken for the recipient's reply. [] copies nobody by default.
outreach.guidance: Owner, 2026-09-27: "in the universal segment there should be a widget to send mail to them". Universal leads come from Apollo, not a harvest, so there are no templates and nothing is drafted: a person picks leads (Leads page, or one lead) and writes one email with {{first_name}} and {{company}} in it (tools/outreach_compose.py). The page shows how it reads for each of them; approving it is the same gate as everywhere -- one approved email per company, checked like an approved draft -- and it goes out from the writer's own Gmail (send_from approver, linked by the owner with tools/users.py gmail), inside that address's daily limit, which it shares with every other project. A lead still in To review is shortlisted by being written to. Replies land in Outreach -> Replies.

apollo.guidance: The five endpoints the Universal page calls, and the only ones a scoped Apollo key needs (Apollo: Settings > Integrations > API Keys > Create new key; a master key also works). Costs, from docs.apollo.io on 2026-09-19: people search 0 credits; company search 1 credit per page of up to 100; bulk_match 1 credit per person Apollo has data for, 0 for a miss; usage stats and profile 0. Personal emails and phone numbers are never requested. max_reveal_per_save caps one save, so a slip of the select-all box cannot spend hundreds of credits at once; the page asks before every save that costs credits.

sourcing.guidance: Owner decision 2026-10-19: all new leads and contacts come from Apollo. Existing project constraints, gates and scoring remain. Company websites and news verify already-known leads; they do not discover new ones. Clipping is exempt.

enrichment.guidance: Apollo supplies new contacts in the target roles. Existing score, geographic and site-verification restrictions and credit caps apply. Websites are read only for qualification evidence.
